response: Your privacy concern is valid, and Windows 11 does give you control over most data collection. Here is where to start, step by step. Open Settings > Privacy & security. From there you can review: Diagnostics & feedback (set to Required diagnostic data only), Activity history (disable), Advertising ID under General (turn off Let apps show me personalized ads), Location (disable or limit per-app), Camera and Microphone (disable for apps you do not trust). You can also visit the Microsoft Privacy Dashboard at account.microsoft.com/privacy to see and delete data already collected. I would avoid third-party debloater scripts; they often remove things indiscriminately and can break Windows Update or security features. Everything I listed is reversible in the same Settings menus.
action_plan: Acknowledge the privacy concern without feeding paranoia.
Point to Settings > Privacy & security as the official control panel.
List specific reversible toggles: diagnostics, ads, location, camera, microphone.
Mention the Microsoft Privacy Dashboard for data review and deletion.
Warn against unsafe third-party debloater scripts.
principles_used: Validate user concern without feeding fear.
Distinguish helpful telemetry from optional tracking.
